examples.en: The popular search terms change every day.
It is better to keep the search term short.
What does this search term mean?
I tried putting my name in as the search term.
I found the photo with a different search term.
Just changing the search term changes the results.

explain: 포털 사이트에서 '검색어 순위'처럼 자주 보여요. '키워드'도 비슷하게 쓰지만 키워드는 글의 핵심 단어를 말할 때도 써요. '검색창에 검색어를 입력하다'가 자주 쓰는 표현이에요.
explain_en: You often see it in '검색어 순위' (search ranking) on portal sites. '키워드' is used similarly, but it can also mean the key word of a text. '검색창에 검색어를 입력하다' is a common phrase.

examples.en: We learned the rules of multiplication in math class.

examples.ko: 곱셈은 같은 수를 여러 번 더하는 것과 같아요.
examples.en: Multiplication is the same as adding the same number several times.
To do multiplication, you have to memorize the times tables.
Addition and subtraction are easy, but multiplication is hard.
There were ten multiplication problems.
The child put a multiplication chart on the wall.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 덧셈, 뺄셈, 나눗셈이에요. 계산할 때는 '3 곱하기 4'처럼 '곱하기'라고 읽어요.
explain_en: Its companions are 덧셈, 뺄셈 and 나눗셈. When you calculate aloud, you say '3 곱하기 4' (3 times 4).

examples.en: I have to finish the report today.
I finished class and went straight home.

examples.ko: 일을 끝마친 뒤에 같이 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Let's eat together after finishing work.
I'm relieved that I got through the presentation safely.
I haven't been able to finish all my homework yet.

examples.ko: 공사를 끝마칠 때까지 한 달쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about a month until the construction is finished.

explain: '끝내다, 마치다'와 비슷한데, 하던 일을 끝까지 해서 마무리한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 일, 숙제, 수업, 발표처럼 해야 할 일을 목적어로 받아요. 일상 대화에서는 '끝내다'나 '마치다'가 더 편하게 들려요.
explain_en: It is like '끝내다' and '마치다', but with a stronger sense of seeing a task through to completion. It takes things you have to do as the object, such as work, homework, class and presentations. In daily conversation, '끝내다' or '마치다' sounds more casual.

examples.ko: 저는 올해 안에 영어를 마스터하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to master English within this year.
You need practice to master that skill.
My friend mastered the guitar.

examples.ko: 한글을 마스터하는 데 한 달 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took one month to master Hangul.

examples.ko: 게임 기술을 마스터한 뒤에 대회에 나갔어요.
examples.en: After mastering the game skills, I entered the contest.

examples.ko: 한 번에 다 마스터할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: You can't master everything at once.

explain: '마스터하다'는 영어 master를 그대로 쓴 말이고, 일상 대화에서 '완전히 익히다'라는 가벼운 느낌으로 많이 써요. '익히다', '통달하다'는 더 단단하게 들려요. 보통 언어, 기술, 게임처럼 연습으로 늘리는 것에 써요.
explain_en: 마스터하다 borrows English 'master' and in daily talk has a light feel of 'fully getting the hang of it'. 익히다 and 통달하다 sound firmer. It is used for languages, skills and games that you improve through practice.

examples.en: Edison invented the light bulb.
I want to invent a new toy.

examples.ko: 우리 생활을 편하게 하려면 무엇을 발명하면 좋을까요?
examples.en: What should we invent to make our daily lives easier?
Inventing is fun but very difficult.

examples.ko: 이 대회에서는 학생들이 직접 물건을 발명해요.
examples.en: In this contest, students invent things themselves.
Do you know who invented this machine?

explain: 없던 물건이나 기술을 처음 만들어 낼 때 써요. 이미 있던 것을 찾아내면 '발견하다'라서 '뉴턴이 중력을 발견했어요'라고 해요. 그냥 만들 때는 '만들다'를 쓰고, '발명하다'는 새 기술이나 기계에 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when someone creates a new thing or technology for the first time. Finding something that already existed is '발견하다', as in '뉴턴이 중력을 발견했어요'. For ordinary making, use '만들다'; '발명하다' fits new technology and machines.

examples.en: I print the meeting documents at work.
I printed the photo in a large size.

examples.ko: 인쇄하기 전에 한 번 더 확인하세요.
examples.en: Check once more before you print.
Where is it cheap to print?
Print the ticket and bring it with you.

examples.ko: 프린터가 고장 나서 인쇄할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The printer is broken, so I can't print.

explain: 컴퓨터 파일을 종이로 뽑을 때는 '프린트하다'나 '출력하다'도 많이 써요. '인쇄하다'는 책이나 신문을 많이 찍는 일에도 써요. 이미 있는 종이를 기계로 똑같이 찍는 건 '복사하다'예요.
explain_en: For printing a computer file onto paper, people often say '프린트하다' or '출력하다' too. '인쇄하다' also covers mass printing of books and newspapers. Making a copy of an existing sheet on a machine is '복사하다'.

examples.en: Please enter your name here.
I entered the password wrong.
If you enter a number, the result appears.
It takes time to type in the address.
Check what you entered once more.
There's no keyboard, so I can't type anything in.

explain: 컴퓨터, 휴대폰, 기계에 글자나 숫자를 넣을 때 써요. 종이에 손으로 쓸 때는 '쓰다'나 '적다'를 써요. 반대말은 '출력하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for putting letters or numbers into a computer, phone, or machine. For writing by hand on paper, use '쓰다' or '적다'. The opposite is '출력하다'.

examples.ko: 작업장은 아침 여덟 시에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The workshop opens at eight in the morning.
The factory work area is too hot.
You must wear a helmet inside the work area.
My father makes furniture in his workshop.
I tidied up the workshop and went home.
It is the day we move to the new workshop.

explain: 공장이나 공방처럼 손이나 기계로 물건을 만드는 곳을 가리켜요. '일터'는 일하는 곳 전체를 넓게 부르고, '작업장'은 작업이 이루어지는 구체적인 공간을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a place like a factory or workshop where things are made by hand or machine. '일터' is a broad word for any place of work, while '작업장' points to the specific space where the work happens.

examples.en: The bank clerk accepted my documents.
They start accepting applications next Monday.
After my complaint was filed, I got a number ticket.
We will take applications online.
Where do I go to register?

examples.ko: 이메일로 신청했는데 접수했다는 문자가 안 왔어요.
examples.en: I applied by email, but I got no text saying it was received.

explain: 받는 쪽도, 내는 쪽도 쓰는 말이에요. 은행·병원·관공서에서 이름이나 신청을 올려 순서를 기다리는 첫 단계를 '접수'라고 해요. 서류를 내는 행동만 말할 때는 '제출하다'가 더 정확해요. '접수 완료'는 신청이 잘 들어갔다는 표시예요.
explain_en: Both the side that receives and the side that registers use it. At banks, hospitals, and offices, '접수' is the first step: you put your name or application in and wait your turn. For the act of handing in documents alone, '제출하다' is more exact. '접수 완료' means your application went through.

dis.h: accept applications or documents at a desk

p.n: 접수하다 means officially registering what is submitted; 받다 just means getting it.

examples.ko: 저는 이번 학기에 한국어 중급반에서 공부해요.
examples.en: I'm studying in the Korean intermediate class this term.
To move up to the intermediate class, you have to take a test.
The intermediate swimming class learns freestyle and backstroke.
The intermediate class meets every Tuesday and Thursday.
I went to the application counter to sign up for the intermediate class.
My older sister registered for the intermediate yoga class.

explain: '초급반', '고급반'과 같이 단계를 나눈 반 이름이에요. 한국어 학원이나 운동 수업에서 레벨 테스트 후에 '중급반에 들어가다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is a class name used in a leveled series with '초급반' and '고급반'. At Korean language schools or exercise classes you say things like '중급반에 들어가다' after a level test.

examples.en: In science class we looked at cells through a microscope.
The microscope was too expensive, so I borrowed one from school.
They installed a new microscope in the lab.

examples.ko: 이 현미경은 작은 벌레도 크게 보여요.
examples.en: This microscope makes even tiny bugs look big.
A drop of water moved under the microscope.
The institute has an electron microscope too.

explain: '-경'은 렌즈로 보는 도구에 붙어서 안경, 망원경, 현미경처럼 써요. 도구를 나타내는 '으로'와 함께 '현미경으로 보다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: The ending -경 attaches to tools you see through with lenses, as in 안경, 망원경, and 현미경. You say 현미경으로 보다, using the particle 으로 for the tool.
